name:
Example: 
                    Finding a Formula for the Nth Term of a Geometric Sequence
problem: Find the formula for the $n$th term of a sequence if the $6$th term is $80$ and the common ratio is $-2.$
worked_solution:
The common ratio is $r=-2,$ so we can start writing the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & ={a}_{1}\cdot (-2)^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

However, we still need to figure out the first term $a_1.$ We know that the $6$th term is $a_6=80,$ so we can solve for the first term as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{6} & ={a}_{1}\cdot (-2)^{6-1} \\ 80 & ={a}_{1}\cdot (-2)^{5} \\ 80 & ={a}_{1}\cdot (-32) \\ -\frac{80}{32} & ={a}_{1} \\ -\frac{5}{2} & ={a}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we know the first term is $a_1=-\dfrac{5}{2},$ we can complete the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot (-2)^{n-1} \\  & =-\frac{5}{2}\cdot (-2)^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify a bit further by manipulating the exponents, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-\frac{5}{2}(-2)^{n-1} \\  & =5\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})\cdot (-2)^{n-1} \\  & =5\cdot (-2)^{-1}\cdot (-2)^{n-1} \\  & =5\cdot (-2)^{n-2}\end{aligned}
$$
